verdict.rationale: Zep's Graphiti framework documents a bi-temporal model and fact invalidation, tracking how facts change over time. This is a first-party mechanism for retiring stale facts, but the evidence describes it only in one-line mentions. No developer-configurable TTL, expiration date, or recency-weighted decay is documented, and manual node/edge deletion is an adjacent control that earns no credit. missing for 10: developer-set TTL or expiration dates on memories, recency weighting or decay in retrieval, documentation that invalidated facts are excluded from search results, hands-on corroboration

support.subject: As a developer, I can make memories expire or decay — via TTL, expiration dates, or recency weighting — so stale facts stop surfacing

citations.quote: entity and edge extraction, the bi-temporal model, fact invalidation, and hybrid retrieval
Unlike static knowledge graphs, Graphiti's context graphs track how facts change over time
